newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude grades steady in rangebound market.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude grades steady in rangebound market.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices remained steady Tuesday afternoon, taking a breather from recent price volatility.

September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing stood slightly weaker from Monday price levels, around unchanged at $20.70-80 a barrel. The September/October spread came back to around -10/7 cents from a midday spurt out to -15/17 cents.

Grade barrels mirrored the lack of price movement in the outright market, traders said. Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James is currently talked at a 22-25 cents premium to the WTI benchmark, within trading levels posted earlier Tuesday.
West Texas Sour/Midland hovered at either side of a $1.35 discount, with Eugene Island at similar levels.
WTI/Cushing Postings Plus held at a $1.95 value, a touch higher than trading levels seen before the afternoon began.
Midland/WTI was pegged at 26-28 cents below WTI, and the Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire at either side of a 20 cents discount, traders said.
Outright prices fluctuated with the NYMEX performance, which failed to move from a $20.55-$20.85 trading range for September crude futures.

Iraq news focused on the waiting game for an announcement of when Baghdad will deliver its pricing formula to U.N. overseers, cementing the final phase of the "oil-for-food" accord. Once the overseers and sanctions committee members approve the price mechanism, Iraq can start selling oil again.
